text:
“You know, I had a family, a job, something

was always

in the way

but now

I sold my house, found this

place, a large studio,

you should see the space and the light.


For the first time in my life I’m going to have the place

and the time to

create”


No, kid, if you’re going to create

you’re going to create while working

16 hours a day in a coal mine

or

you’re going to create in a tiny room with three kids

while you’re

unemployed,

you’re going to create even if part of your mind and

your body is missing, you’re going to create blind, maimed, crazy,

you’re going to create with a cat climbing up your

back while

the whole city trembles in earthquakes,

bombings, floods, and fire.


Kid, air, light, time and space

have nothing to do with this

and create nothing

except perhaps a longer life in which to find

new excuses.

translation.title: Air, Light, Time and Space
translation.editorial_note: Translated from the supplied Spanish version of Charles Bukowski. The conversational register, quotation marks, repeated “you’re going to create,” and lineation are preserved.
